source.paraphrase: useFetch and useAsyncData run once on the server and replay on the client. A bare fetch runs twice and can disagree.

invariants.why: A bare fetch in pages, components, or composables double-fires across SSR and hydration and skips the shared payload cache.
invariants.fixHint: Replace fetch with useFetch or useAsyncData with a stable key so the server result replays on the client.
invariants.avoid: Calling fetch through globalThis does not change the call. The receiver is not the rule; the fetch is.

source.paraphrase: Runtime config separates private server values from public client values. process.env has no such split in app code.

invariants.why: Reading process.env in app code either inlines secrets into the client bundle or silently yields undefined where the build did not inject it.
invariants.fixHint: Expose the value through runtimeConfig and read it with useRuntimeConfig in app code.
invariants.avoid: Subscript access does not hide the read. process.env["X"] is the same environment read as process.env.X.

source.paraphrase: useState without a key returns one shared ref for every caller. The key is what separates independent state.

invariants.why: An unkeyed useState merges every component instance into one slot, so one cart, counter, or form overwrites another.
invariants.fixHint: Pass a unique string key and an initializer: useState("cart", () => []).
invariants.avoid: Type arguments do not key the state. useState<string>() without a key still shares one slot.

source.paraphrase: Setup code runs on both server and client and must produce the same tree. Nondeterministic values render twice and mismatch.

invariants.why: Math.random and Date.now in setup code produce one value on the server and another on the client, so hydration patches or warns on every load.
invariants.fixHint: Generate the value on the server and pass it down, or generate it after mount where only the client renders it.
invariants.avoid: A lazy initializer does not defer past setup. useState("k", () => Date.now()) still stamps during SSR.

source.locator: navigateTo usage note; Within route middleware; middleware return values
source.paraphrase: Always await or return the result of navigateTo. In route middleware a redirect or cancellation happens only when navigateTo or abortNavigation is returned.

invariants.why: A discarded navigateTo in middleware lets the original navigation continue, so the guarded page renders for a user who should have been redirected.
invariants.fixHint: Write return navigateTo("/login") or return abortNavigation() in middleware, and await navigateTo(...) in handlers and composables.
invariants.avoid: Putting the call on one arm of an if does not return it. An arrow with an expression body already returns its value and is not matched.

source.paraphrase: The handler must return a truthy value, not undefined or null, or the request may be duplicated on the client.

invariants.why: A handler that only fills a store or ref resolves to undefined, so the payload carries nothing and the client fetches the same data again during hydration.
invariants.fixHint: Return the fetched data. When the handler only fills a store, return true after the store action.
invariants.avoid: A return inside a nested callback, or a bare return, does not give the handler a value. Named handler references and expression-bodied arrows are not matched.

source.paraphrase: process.browser, process.client, process.dev, process.server and process.test are soft-deprecated since Nuxt 3.12. Prefer the matching import.meta flags.

invariants.why: The process flags only exist through a compatibility define; newer Nuxt drops their types, so the branch stops type-checking and confuses server and client builds.
invariants.fixHint: Replace process.client with import.meta.client, process.server with import.meta.server and process.dev with import.meta.dev.
invariants.avoid: process.browser is the same deprecated flag under its Nuxt 2 name. process.env is a separate rule (NUXT-ENV-001).
